widgets.name: Keycap
widgets.purpose: A button that shows one shortcut binding as keycap glyphs in a settings row and, when activated, records the next key combo for that action. Idle and recording are one component on a mode axis because they share the box, radius, font and focus handling. The reset control is a sibling button beside the keycap, never nested inside it. Sizes at 1rem = 14px (reference from A): height 21px = 1.5rem; idle minimum width 49px = 3.5rem, content width otherwise; recording fixed width 101px = 7.214rem; radius 4.375px = 0.3125rem, which is the radius-sm token; label text 11px = 0.786rem on a 16.5px = 1.179rem line. MERGE NOTES: Sources are A (reference capture) and B (shadcn consolidation). A's 52px (3.714rem) idle width for three-glyph combos is dropped as a separate size and folded into content width above the 3.5rem minimum (B), because a 3px difference is not a distinction a user feels. B's label prop is dropped as a duplicate of actionName. B's binding prop is dropped as a duplicate of accel. B's custom boolean is dropped and folded into the binding variant value custom, which keeps A's visible reset-control distinction. B's onRecordStart and onRecordCancel are dropped as duplicates of A's onStartRecording and onCancel. A's onUnbind is folded into onCapture(null) (B), because the split is an API detail a user cannot see. The 'disabled' prop and state come from B only and are kept as library additions outside the reference.
widgets.base: shadcn/ui Button pattern (secondary-style surface, no Radix primitive; A calls it a custom control on the library's button element), rendered as a native button. In idle mode it composes HotkeyHint (size sm, tone inherit) for the glyphs. In recording mode the HotkeyHint child is removed. The root is a group element (B) so the reset IconButton can sit beside the keycap without nesting interactive elements.

values.when: Default. Muted fill: reference surface oklch(0.944 0.003 255) mapped to the muted token. Text: reference oklch(0.46 0.013 262) mapped to muted-foreground. Shows HotkeyHint sm, tone inherit, for the accel, or the unboundLabel text when accel is empty. Width is a 3.5rem (49px) minimum and content width otherwise.

Used only on the row being edited, and only one row at a time (the owning list enforces this). HotkeyHint and glyphs are removed and the prompt is shown. Fixed width 101px = 7.214rem. Reference text colour is accent blue oklch(0.6 0.2 255) with a thin blue outline (width not measured); this build replaces the blue with foreground text and the shared neutral focus ring outline pending open item 1. accel is ignored while recording.
Binding equals the built-in default. No reset control rendered.
Binding has been customised. The reset control (shared ghost IconButton, sibling of the keycap) is shown beside the keycap. Reset look, size and position are open (see open items).
accel is empty or null. Shows the unboundLabel text (default None) in muted text in place of glyphs.

props.name: mode
props.description: Variant axis. Controlled by the owning list, which holds the editor state. Only one keycap in a list is in recording mode at a time.

props.name: binding
props.description: Variant axis for binding content, derived by the owner: unbound when accel is empty or null, custom when the binding has been customised, otherwise default. Ignored in recording mode. Replaces B's custom boolean.

props.name: accel
props.description: Current accelerator for the row. Empty or null means unbound. Stored format is defined by the binding store and is not yet specified (see open items). Kept from A; B's binding prop is the same job and is dropped.

props.name: actionName
props.description: Name of the command the row binds. Used in the accessible name. Kept from A; B's label prop is the same job and is dropped.

props.name: prompt
props.description: Text shown while recording. Reference English text; needs a localisation key (open item).

props.name: unboundLabel
props.description: Text shown when unbound. Reference English text; needs a localisation key (open item).

props.name: onStartRecording
props.description: Called on activation when idle. The owning list then sets mode to recording. Kept from A; B's onRecordStart is a duplicate and is dropped.

props.name: onCapture
props.description: Called with the captured combo while recording. Called with null when a bare Backspace or Delete unbinds the row (B consolidation of A's onCapture and onUnbind). A's onUnbind is folded into this callback.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Called on Escape, or on a second activation of the recording keycap. Kept from A; B's onRecordCancel is a duplicate and is dropped.

props.name: onReset
props.description: Restores the default binding. Called from the reset control, which is rendered only when binding is custom.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Library addition from B, not in the reference capture. Disables activation and styling.

states: idle + custom (reset control shown beside the keycap)
hover (not in reference capture; B proposes foreground text on a slightly darker muted fill, values to confirm)
focus-visible (reference look not captured; uses the shared neutral focus ring token, not accent blue)
widgets.role: button for the keycap. Accessible name is actionName plus the spelled-out accel, for example 'Delete task, Backspace, press to change' (B example). aria-keyshortcuts carries accel (proposed, A). group for the wrapper that holds the optional reset control (B). While recording, the prompt is announced through a polite live region (proposed in A, also in B).
widgets.keyboard: Tab moves focus to the keycap. The reset control is a separate Tab stop after the keycap and activates with Enter or Space (B). Enter or Space starts recording (native button activation; the reference documents only click, so this is proposed). While recording, keydowns are captured and default-prevented so app shortcuts do not fire, except that Tab is proposed (A) to pass through and cancel (open item; this is an exception to B's every-keydown rule). Escape cancels. Bare Backspace or Delete calls onCapture(null) to unbind. Any other combo calls onCapture(accel). Activating the keycap again (click, Enter or Space) cancels; the click cancel is from the reference at useHotkeyEditor.ts:121-124. Blur cancelling is not in the reference (proposed yes, open item).
widgets.platform: Same component on both platforms. Web: recording sees only keys the page receives. Browser-reserved combos (for example Ctrl/Cmd+T, W, N, and Cmd+N, Cmd+W, Cmd+T on macOS) never reach the page, so recording must reject or warn (proposed in A; B asks for block, warn or accept). Web has no global hotkeys, so recorded accelerators are in-app only. Capture bar, screenshot and clear-capture-draft rows do not exist on web (no capture window, no screenshots). Desktop: capture is in the focused main window. A global hotkey pressed while the main window is focused is captured as the new combo and does not fire (inferred in A, not stated in the catalogue). Desktop bindings may be global hotkeys (B); OS-reserved combos cannot be captured. If settings runs in its own window, Escape cancels recording and must not close that window (B).
widgets.open: 1) Recording colour and accent use: the reference draws recording text and outline in accent blue oklch(0.6 0.2 255). Accent blue is reserved for primary action and selection, so this build proposes foreground text plus the neutral ring (B). A token is needed before the library ships. Confirm. 2) Hover and focus-visible looks are not in the captured tree; proposed hover is foreground text on a slightly darker muted fill, and focus uses the shared neutral ring token (B). Values to confirm; keyboard use needs a visible focus state. 3) Reset control look, size and position are not captured. It is a shared ghost IconButton (B) and must be a sibling of the keycap, not nested. Confirm neutral ghost rather than danger, since restoring a default is not destructive (B). 4) The strings None and Type shortcut… are English reference text and need localisation keys. 5) Not in the reference: whether Tab is captured during recording (proposed: Tab passes through and cancels, A), whether blur cancels recording (proposed yes, A and B), and whether a bare modifier keydown (for example Shift alone) completes a recording (B; not stated in the catalogue). 6) Web: should a browser-reserved combo be blocked, warned about, or accepted when recorded (A proposes reject or warn, B asks). 7) Desktop: Escape inside a dialog or settings window must cancel recording only (B, to confirm). Whether a combo recorded here that is also a global hotkey (for example screenshot capture) is registered globally is not in the catalogue (A). 8) Stored accel format is defined by the binding store and is not yet specified (A, B).

widgets.name: HotkeyHint
widgets.purpose: Display-only glyph sequence for one accelerator. It draws the platform modifier glyph, the Option or Alt glyph, and the key glyph in the order the catalogue gives, edge to edge. It is used inside Keycap, in the command palette row, and on capture bar buttons, so one job uses one widget everywhere. Sizes at 1rem = 14px (from A and B): sm uses 12px glyphs = 0.857rem, weight 300; md uses 13px modifier glyphs (0.929rem) with 13px key letters in this build, on an 18px = 1.286rem line. MERGE NOTES: Sources are A (reference capture) and B (shadcn consolidation). A's mixed md sizes (13px modifier glyphs, 12px letters) are folded to one 13px rule (B) because the 1px letter difference is not a user-felt size change; A's 12px letters are recorded here and listed in open items. B's palette icon weight 400 is folded to glyph weight 300 to match the other two hints (B). A's platform values macos|windows|other are kept over B's mac|windows|linux, since 'other' covers Linux. B's palette letter fold and A's reference size are both kept as open items. Two props from A and B are identical (accel, size, tone, platform) and are not duplicated.
widgets.base: shadcn/ui Kbd pattern: a kbd element extended with platform glyph mapping (B). A lists the base as none (display element with kbd as the natural host). No Radix primitive.

values.when: 12px glyphs and text (0.857rem), weight 300. Used inside the settings Keycap (idle) and on the capture bar Clear and screenshot buttons (capture bar font 12px/12px).

13px glyphs and text (0.929rem), weight 300. Used only in command palette rows, where the reference calls it the larger size. Takes the row colour, so it changes with the active row. Reference key letters were 12px on an 18px = 1.286rem line; folded to 13px per B, see open items.

Uses currentColor, so it takes the parent's text colour. Settings keycap: oklch(0.46 0.013 262). Palette row: the row colour, oklch(0.62 0.013 264) in default rows, changing with the active row. Reads as part of its container.
Muted-foreground token, oklch(0.62 0.013 264) in light mode. Used on the capture bar Clear and screenshot buttons. The dark-mode value differs in the reference and is open (see open items).

props.name: accel
props.description: Canonical accelerator (modifiers plus key) from the binding store. Stored format is not yet defined. An empty value renders nothing (proposed in A). The consumer renders the widget only when an accelerator exists (palette rows) or in the stated capture-bar states.

props.name: size
props.description: Glyph and text size from the size axis. Default sm.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colour from the tone axis. Default inherit.

props.name: platform
props.description: Host OS, from app context by default (B), used to resolve glyphs: Command and Option on macOS; Control and Alt on Windows and web. 'other' covers Linux, whose glyph map is not in the brief (A kept; B's 'mac' | 'windows' | 'linux' is a naming alternative, see open items).

states: md + inherit (command palette row, follows active row)
sm + muted (capture bar Clear and screenshot buttons)
not shown, consumer rule: palette rows without an accelerator
not shown, consumer rule: capture-bar Clear hint unless the Clear button is shown
not shown, consumer rule: screenshot hint except in idle, and not while capturing or on error
widgets.role: none. Renders a kbd element with aria-hidden glyphs and a visually hidden text equivalent, for example 'Command Shift N' or 'Command Shift H', so a screen reader reads the shortcut and not glyph names (proposed, A and B).
widgets.platform: Glyph resolution differs by platform. macOS: Command glyph (keyboard_command_key) and Option glyph (keyboard_option_key). Windows: Control glyph for the Command modifier (inferred from Control-click; the shortcut mapping is not stated, so confirm) and Alt for Option. Web follows the same rule as Windows for Command and Alt for Option, per the decision (A). Linux glyph map is not in the brief. Capture-bar hints are desktop only. Palette rows on web must not show accelerators that browsers reserve (for example N, F, Shift+N), see open items.
widgets.open: 1) Confirm the Command to Control glyph mapping on Windows and web (A). 2) The Linux glyph map and the canonical accelerator format are not in the brief; confirm whether 'other' covers Linux or a separate 'linux' value is needed (A, B). 3) Muted dark-mode value: the reference records oklch(0.57 0.011 262) only for the screenshot hint, and that is uncertain. Decide one token or two; B folds both into one muted-foreground token (A, B). 4) Palette md sizes: reference uses 13px modifier glyphs with 12px key letters on an 18px line; B folds letters to 13px. Confirm visually, and revert to 12px letters if the palette rhythm suffers (A, B). The palette icon weight 400 in the reference is folded to 300 (B); confirm. 5) Glyph names in the reference are Material Symbols style (keyboard_command_key, keyboard_option_key, keyboard_return, backspace, arrow_upward, arrow_back). The text-key mapping (N, F, Z, comma, backslash, minus) must be confirmed (A). 6) Palette accelerators that browsers commonly reserve on web (N, F, Shift+N) need a product decision: drop them or mark them on web (A, B). 7) Consumer rules sit outside this widget: the capture-bar screenshot hint is shown only in the idle state, and the Clear hint only with the Clear button (A, B).
